summary: Available sources point to illegal sand transport on the Shahjahanpur Road, crime and police action in Nakur town, and sugarcane dues tied to the Sarsawa mill, while water, road and power complaints could not be verified for this AC.

positives.basis: Nakur news feed headline dated 29 Jul 2026: 'मुठभेड के बाद पुलिस ने किये तीन आरोपी बदमाश किये गिरफ्तार' (police arrested three accused after an encounter). The source reports arrests only, not voter satisfaction.

positives.english: The Sarsawa sugar mill has paid cane farmers before

positives.english: Nakur, Sarsawa and Sultanpur have municipal bodies that run local civic work

positives.basis: Inference: Wikipedia lists the Nakur and Sarsawa NPPs and the Chilkana Sultanpur NP inside the AC. Whether civic work is effective was not verified.

negatives.english: Sugarcane farmers wait months for dues from the mills
negatives.hindi: गन्ने का पैसा मिलों से महीनों देर से मिलता है, किसान परेशान
negatives.basis: Inference: Amar Ujala (3 Jun 2021, district-level) says the district's mills still owed farmers Rs 630 crore after paying Rs 100.34 crore that day, with Sarsawa and Nanauta mills named. This is 2021 data; no 2024-26 Saharanpur or Nakur dues report was found, so current arrears are unverified.

negatives.basis: Inference: Nakur news feed (20 Feb 2026) reports police and revenue officials seized a sand-laden truck on the Shahjahanpur Road that lacked documents. The source reports the seizure, not a voter complaint; road damage and safety concerns are not stated.

notes: Identity confirmed from the Wikipedia AC page (AC No. 2, Nakur, Saharanpur district, reserved status None). The Election Commission list was not checked directly. The Hindi name 'नकुड़' is taken from local-news spelling because the Wikipedia page gives no Hindi name. Research is incomplete: the web search budget for this session ran out after about 13 WebSearch calls, so the 15+ target was not met and several planned Hindi queries (water, electricity, roads, stray cattle, Sarsawa and Nakur hospital, Nakur sugar dues 2025-26) were not run. Only four source URLs were opened: the Wikipedia AC page, the Amar Ujala 2021 sugar-dues article, and the Public App Nakur news feed (headlines quoted from that page, outlets not identified). The Public App feed is an aggregator, so the underlying Hindi outlets should be checked before publishing. Positives 3-5 and negatives 4-5 are inference with no AC-specific evidence. Electoral data (vote counts, margins, MLA result details) was left out per the brief. Field check recommended: Amar Ujala and Dainik Jagran Saharanpur pages for नकुड़, सरसावा, सुल्तानपुर and चिलकाना on water, power, roads, cane dues (2025-26) and stray cattle; Nakur sand-mining complaints on the Krishni river; the Nakur CHC; and the 2023 Gurjar rally internet suspension, which appeared in search results but was not opened.
